mnemonic.meaning: Two kanji that both mean arrive (到, 着): you reach the gate, and you're really there. Arrival.
mnemonic.reading: Your TOE hits the CHALK line (とうちゃく) at the finish. Arrival!

examples.ja: 飛行機は予定より三十分早く到着した。
examples.en: The plane arrived thirty minutes earlier than scheduled.

items.note: 到着 = arrival. The opposite is 出発 (しゅっぱつ).

mnemonic.meaning: You go all the way through (徹) the night (夜) without sleeping. Staying up all night.
mnemonic.reading: Your friend TETSUYA (てつや) is famous for one thing: he never sleeps. Every exam, another all-nighter.

examples.ja: 試験の前の日に徹夜して勉強した。
examples.en: I stayed up all night studying the day before the exam.

items.note: 徹夜する = stay up all night. 夜 is や here (usually よる).

mnemonic.meaning: You pull (引) all your boxes and cross over (越) to a new place. Moving house.
mnemonic.reading: Moving day: you HICCUP and COACH (ひっこし) the movers through the door.

examples.ja: 来月、大阪へ引越しすることになった。
examples.en: It's been decided that I'm moving to Osaka next month.

items.note: Also written 引っ越し. The verb is 引っ越す.

mnemonic.meaning: 眺 has 目 (eye): your eyes rest on the far-off view. You gaze at it.
mnemonic.reading: NAG, A MAN RUE (ながめる)? No, he just sits by the window gazing at the sea.

examples.ja: 窓から海を眺めるのが好きだ。
examples.en: I like looking out at the sea from the window.

items.note: 眺める = look at something for a while, like a view or the sky.

mnemonic.meaning: 握 has 扌 (hand): your hand closes tight around something. To grip.
mnemonic.reading: KNEE GEAR (にぎる): you grip the handlebars so hard your knee gear rattles.

examples.ja: 子どもは母親の手を強く握った。
examples.en: The child gripped his mother's hand tightly.

items.note: 握る = grip or squeeze. 握手 (あくしゅ) = handshake.

mnemonic.meaning: 溜 has 氵 (water): water collects and builds up in a puddle. To pile up.
mnemonic.reading: TOMATO RUE (たまる): unwashed tomatoes pile up in the sink until you regret it.

examples.ja: 掃除しないと、部屋にほこりが溜まる。
examples.en: If you don't clean, dust builds up in the room.

items.note: 溜まる = something builds up. 溜める = you save it up.

mnemonic.meaning: 嫌 has 女 (woman): she clearly dislikes the guy talking to her.
mnemonic.reading: KEY, RAW (きらう)! Your sister dislikes raw fish so much she locks the fridge with a key.

examples.ja: 猫は水を嫌う。
examples.en: Cats dislike water.

items.note: 嫌う = dislike (verb). Everyday speech usually says 嫌いだ.

mnemonic.meaning: One (一) blink (瞬). That's how long it lasts: an instant.
mnemonic.reading: "EAT SHOE-N (いっしゅん)!" In an instant, the dog grabs your shoe.

examples.ja: 一瞬、何が起きたのかわからなかった。
examples.en: For a moment, I didn't know what had happened.

items.note: 一瞬 = an instant. 瞬間 (しゅんかん) = the exact moment something happens.

mnemonic.meaning: 抱 has 扌 (hand) wrapping around something: you hold it in your arms. You also hold problems and work.
mnemonic.reading: CAW-CAW, AIR RUE (かかえる): you hold a crow in your arms and it won't stop cawing. What a problem to have.

examples.ja: 両手で荷物を抱えるのは大変だ。
examples.en: Carrying luggage in both arms is hard.

items.note: 抱える = hold in your arms; also to carry a burden. 問題を抱える = have problems.

mnemonic.meaning: 輝 has 光 (light): light bouncing off something. To shine, to sparkle.
mnemonic.reading: CAR GUY, YAK (かがやく): the car guy polishes his car with yak wool until it sparkles.

examples.ja: 夜空に星が輝く。
examples.en: Stars shine in the night sky.

items.note: 輝く = shine brightly: stars, eyes, a future. 光る (ひかる) = give off light.

mnemonic.meaning: 願 has 頁 (head): you bow your head and make a wish.
mnemonic.reading: NEIGH, GOW (ねがう)! A horse neighs at a shooting star. It wishes for an apple.

examples.ja: 家族の健康を願う。
examples.en: I wish for my family's health.

items.note: 願う = wish or hope. お願いします comes from this verb.

mnemonic.meaning: Now (今) and after (後): from now on, in the future.
mnemonic.reading: CON GO (こんご)! From now on, the con man has to go straight.

examples.ja: 今後はもっと気をつけます。
examples.en: From now on, I'll be more careful.

items.note: 今後 = from now on (a bit formal). 今度 (こんど) = this time or next time.

mnemonic.meaning: The amount that's right (当) for both sides (相)... and then some. Considerably, quite a lot.
mnemonic.reading: SO TOE (そうとう)? You stubbed it considerably. It's quite swollen.

examples.ja: 彼は相当疲れているようだ。
examples.en: He seems quite tired.

items.note: 相当 = considerably, like かなり. It can also mean "equivalent to".

mnemonic.meaning: 超 has 走 (run): you run past the line. To exceed, to go over.
mnemonic.reading: A CROW-AIR-RUE (こえる): the crow flies over the fence and exceeds its limits.

examples.ja: 今日の気温は三十五度を超えるそうだ。
examples.en: They say today's temperature will go over 35 degrees.

items.note: 超える = go over a limit or a number. 越える (same reading) = cross over a place.

mnemonic.meaning: Firm (確) reality (実): it's real and it's firm. Certain, reliable.
mnemonic.reading: CACK, GEE-TSU (かくじつ)! The chicken is certain: it lays an egg every morning, reliable as clockwork.

examples.ja: このままでは、遅刻するのは確実だ。
examples.en: At this rate, being late is certain.

items.note: 確実 = certain, sure. 確実に = definitely.

mnemonic.meaning: The right (当) time (時) you're talking about, back then. At that time.
mnemonic.reading: TOE GEE (とうじ): back then, you didn't even have toes this big. At that time you were a baby.

examples.ja: 大学生だった当時、毎日アルバイトをしていた。
examples.en: Back when I was a university student, I worked part-time every day.

items.note: 当時 = back then, at a specific past time. 同時 (どうじ) = at the same time.

mnemonic.meaning: Becoming (成) long (長), taller and bigger. Growth, growing up.
mnemonic.reading: SAY, CHOW (せいちょう)! Eat all your chow and you'll grow up big.

examples.ja: 子どもの成長は本当に早い。
examples.en: Children grow up so fast.

items.note: 成長する = grow up or develop (people, companies, the economy).

mnemonic.meaning: The heart (心) in the middle (中). The center, the core.
mnemonic.reading: CHEW SHIN (ちゅうしん): the dog chews the shin bone right down to the core.

examples.ja: 駅は町の中心にある。
examples.en: The station is in the center of town.

items.note: 中心 = the middle or core of something. 〜を中心に = centered on.

mnemonic.meaning: MARU (circle) DE: "it's all one perfect circle (まるで)!" Just like a full moon. It's as if the cake were the moon.

examples.ja: 彼はまるで子供のように笑った。
examples.en: He laughed just like a child.

items.note: まるで〜ようだ / みたいだ = as if. With a negative it means "not at all": まるで分からない.

mnemonic.meaning: SHE CAME, OH (しかも)... and what's more, she brought dessert! Moreover.

examples.ja: この店は安い。しかも、おいしい。
examples.en: This place is cheap. And what's more, it's tasty.

items.note: Adds a stronger second point: 失敗した。しかも二回も。(I failed, and twice at that.) Also "and yet": 注意された。しかも、また同じ間違いをした。

mnemonic.meaning: 場 has 土 (earth): a patch of ground where something happens. A place, a spot.
mnemonic.reading: BAH (ば)! the sheep says. It knows exactly which spot is its place.

examples.ja: その場ですぐに返事をした。
examples.en: I replied right there on the spot.

items.note: Common in set phrases: その場で (on the spot), 場合 (case). On its own, ば is a bit formal; 場所 is the everyday word.

mnemonic.meaning: SO RAY, ZO RAY (それぞれ): each ray of the sun lands on each kid respectively.

examples.ja: 人にはそれぞれ好みがある。
examples.en: Everyone has their own tastes.

items.note: Often 〜はそれぞれ違う: each one is different. Close to 各自 (かくじ) but more everyday.

mnemonic.meaning: NAN TOE-CAR (なんとか): grandma drives the toy car with her toe, and somehow she manages.

examples.ja: なんとか終電に間に合った。
examples.en: I somehow made the last train.

items.note: なんとかする = do something about it. なんとかなる = it'll work out somehow.

mnemonic.meaning: 件 is 人 (person) + 牛 (cow): a person with a cow is a case for the court. A matter, an affair.
mnemonic.reading: KEN (けん) is the lawyer who handles this case.

examples.ja: その件については、後で話しましょう。
examples.en: Let's talk about that matter later.

items.note: Used a lot at work: この件 (this matter). As a counter it counts cases or emails: 3件.

mnemonic.meaning: 例 has 亻 (person) lined up in a row: each person is an example.
mnemonic.reading: RAY (れい) of light is a perfect example. Teachers always use it as an example.

examples.ja: 例を挙げて説明してください。
examples.en: Please explain with an example.

items.note: 例の + noun = "that ... we talked about": 例の件 (that matter).

mnemonic.meaning: EASY, ZOO RAY (いずれ): sooner or later, the zoo's sunray reaches every animal. Eventually.

examples.ja: いずれ分かる日が来るよ。
examples.en: The day will come when you understand, sooner or later.

items.note: いずれにしても = in any case. いずれ also means "either one" in formal speech.

mnemonic.meaning: MASSAGE NEE (まさに): the masseuse hits exactly the right spot on your knee. Truly perfect.

examples.ja: これはまさに私が探していた本だ。
examples.en: This is exactly the book I was looking for.

items.note: Stronger than ちょうど. Often for emphasis: まさにその通り = exactly right.

mnemonic.meaning: The HOBO (ほぼ) has almost everything he needs. Nearly.

examples.ja: 仕事はほぼ終わった。
examples.en: The work is almost finished.

items.note: A little more formal than だいたい. Common in news: ほぼ毎日 (almost every day).

mnemonic.meaning: One (一) direction (方). On one side it's sunny... on the other hand, it's raining over there.
mnemonic.reading: EAT POH (いっぽう): one side eats, meanwhile the other side watches.

examples.ja: 兄は背が高い。一方、弟は小さい。
examples.en: The older brother is tall. The younger one, on the other hand, is small.

items.note: Also the grammar 〜一方だ (keeps getting more and more).

mnemonic.meaning: 流 has 氵 (water): water moving along. A flow, a current.
mnemonic.reading: NAG A RAY (ながれ): the river nags at the sunrays as it flows past in its current.

examples.ja: 川の流れが速い。
examples.en: The river's current is fast.

items.note: Also used for the flow of time or events: 話の流れ (the flow of a conversation).
